design: Part 1, grouping only (`group`, no assembly) on the three M7 datasets at a 4-sample cap: sketches of the discovery pools and of the original reads with the merge and seeded policies, threshold sensitivity on the pools, and the per-sample hash cap on the hard benchmark's reads. Part 2, hard benchmark coassemblies of the M7 discovery pools at a 4-sample cap: sketch grouping (merge) and three seeded random groupings, against community metadata grouping and one pooled assembly (the M7 runs) and grouped all-read assembly (the M7 gate baseline). 16 threads / 64 GiB, serially, under /usr/bin/time; end-to-end cost includes discovery.

sketch_settings.hash: MurmurHash3 fmix64 of the 2-bit canonical k-mer XOR fmix64(seed); keep hashes <= floor((2^64 - 1) / scaled)
sketch_settings.linkage: average over the neighbour graph (missing links count as 0)
sketch_settings.similarity: Jaccard index of the sketch hashes each sample shares with at least one other sample

evaluation_notes: communities: per-community MetaQUAST as in M7: each arm's contigs from groups containing that community's samples, against the community's source genomes; the gate is per held-out genome against grouped all-read assembly. A grouping that spreads a community over several groups is credited there with several assemblies of a genome shared by all communities, so thin genomes are compared under global_lens: each arm's whole contig output against every source genome. Community and pooled arms and all-read assembly are the M7 runs (same discovery pools, same machine, same settings); their costs are from M7. The adjusted Rand index compares groups with the simulated communities (1 = identical, about 0 = chance).
